summary.oneLiner: Faze Three Limited is an export-oriented Indian manufacturer of home and technical textile furnishing products, supplying global retail giants and wholesalers across 23 countries.
summary.business: Faze Three Limited manufactures home and technical textile furnishing products, including bathmats, bath rugs, area rugs, indoor/outdoor rugs, top-of-the-bed products, blankets, curtains, patio mats and cushions. The Company operates a B2B model and generates over 90% of its turnover from exports to large retailers and wholesalers across the USA, EU and UK, with a dedicated key account manager assigned to each customer.

currentContext.strengths: Exports account for over 90% of turnover, with products supplied to global retail giants and a wide range of vendors/wholesalers across the USA, EU and UK|Diversified product portfolio spanning bathmats, luxury bath rugs, area rugs, indoor/outdoor rugs, bed products, blankets, curtains, patio mats and cushions|B2B model with a dedicated key account manager per customer for 360-degree communication|Promoter-led management with over three decades of textile industry experience (Chairman & Managing Director Ajay Anand; Whole-time Director Sanjay Anand)|CARE Ratings reaffirmed the Company's Long-term & Short-term Bank Facility ratings at A (Stable)/A1 in September 2025
currentContext.strategies: Diversifying into outdoor floor coverings through wholly owned subsidiary Mats and More Private Limited, which has developed and commercialized patio mats|Maintaining a strong R&D pipeline by engaging closely with global retail partners, using customer feedback and market insights to co-create products tailored to international markets|Technological upgrades across weaving, tufting, dyeing and wet-processing machinery aimed at more efficient, cost-effective and environmentally conscious manufacturing|Sustaining a wide array of quality and sustainability certifications (OEKO-TEX Standard 100, OEKO-TEX STeP, GRS, GOTS, OCS, BCI, ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001, Higg FEM, SA8000:2014, SMETA 4-Pillar, SLCP/Higg FSLM, SCAN) to enhance transparency, customer trust and global market access
currentContext.expansion: Faze Three operates a vertically integrated manufacturing platform spanning yarn to finished product across cotton and man-made fibre (MMF) lines, with eight factory locations - two at Silvassa, one at Vapi, four at Panipat and one at Aurangabad - plus a design and sales presence in New York (Faze3 USA LLC). Continued investment across these units has created an installed revenue capacity of over Rs 1,650 crores, with a factory replacement value in excess of Rs 800 crores. The expanded manufacturing capacity at Silvassa spans approximately 106,000 sq. ft. and has been designed with modern infrastructure including Li-ion powered warehouse trucks and forklifts. Over the past four years, the Company has invested across all manufacturing locations to expand capacity in established product lines while introducing new offerings, positioning it to leverage the 'China Plus One' sourcing shift. To strengthen its MMF technology base, the Company has filed an application under the amended Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for MMF, with approval expected in Q1/Q2 of FY 2026-27. On the ESG side, the Company has articulated a long-term decarbonisation process through 2040, with interim objectives including green-building and a progressive increase in the share of renewable energy in its overall energy mix, and states that additional ESG-linked capital expenditure has been committed for the current financial year (quantum not disclosed in this bundle). The Company has invested in 3.5 MW of rooftop solar capacity and clean energy (PNG) for processing, and has developed rainwater harvesting capacity of over 2,000 kilo-litres at its Western India operations.
currentContext.mdna: India continues to benefit from U.S.-led restrictions on Xinjiang-linked Chinese cotton and the global 'China Plus One' sourcing strategy, with global firms expanding sourcing/manufacturing in India, particularly in technical textiles, MMF-based apparel and value-added textile exports|Progress on proposed and ongoing trade agreements with the EU, UK and US is expected to strengthen India's export competitiveness over the medium to long term, with full benefits becoming progressively visible over the next one to two years|The Indian textile industry faced a severe tariff shock in FY26 (US tariffs escalating from 10% to 50% between April and August 2025, lasting nearly six months through early February 2026, coinciding with the peak US Christmas-stocking ordering season), but the same environment strengthened India's relevance in global home and technical textile sourcing via supply-chain diversification by large international retailers|The United States remains India's largest textile export market (over 28-29% of total textile exports), particularly in home textiles|India has consolidated its position as the second-largest exporter of home textiles globally (~7-8% of global trade in the segment), with bed linen, bath towels, curtains and rugs as key categories, and the domestic home textiles industry expected to grow steadily through 2027 on both export and domestic demand|Government support via initiatives such as PM MITRA (Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel) Parks and Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes for MMF, along with the National Technical Textiles Mission, expected to support long-term opportunities for Indian textile manufacturers|EBITDA margins rebounded through FY26 (from a low of 2.66% in Q2FY26 to 13.25% in Q4FY26) on operating leverage from higher revenues, unwinding of tariff-related impacts, a more favorable USD/INR environment and improving sentiment around trade agreements; management remains optimistic that margins will continue to improve as revenues scale further

risks.note: The Company reported its lowest EBITDA margin of the year (2.66%, Q2FY26) primarily due to mark-to-market losses on its USD/INR forward contracts following a sharp rupee depreciation (USD/INR moving from Rs. 85.7 to Rs. 88.8) amid trade-related policy volatility, showing margin sensitivity to currency swings given the Company's export-heavy revenue base.

Consolidated revenue growth in FY26 came despite tariff disruptions throughout April 2025-February 2026 and significant uncertainty affecting industry and global markets, reflecting the Company's exposure as a predominantly export-oriented manufacturer to shifts in trade policy.

one-line thesis: Faze Three is a vertically integrated, order-backed manufacturer of home and technical textiles exporting to top US/EU retailers, uniquely positioned to capture China+1 supply chain shifts due to its scale, 20+ year customer relationships, and low-cost Indian production. With major capex concluding in FY27, it is poised for margin expansion and cash flow inflection as tariffs unwind and PLI approval nears.
financial scorecard / credit view: INR 932.8 Cr / INR 92.27 Cr / INR 33.6 Cr / INR 222.9 Cr (FY26); CARE A (Stable) / A1 — rationale: strong operating leverage, manageable net debt/EBITDA of 2.33x, and asset-backed barrier to entry (replacement cost >INR 800 Cr)
guidance / outlook: Revenue growth to continue in FY27/FY28 with operating leverage; EBIDTA margins to rebound as tariff impacts unwind and scale improves; PLI for MMF approval expected Q1/Q2 FY27; capex cycle concluding FY27 frees 40-50% of CFO for debt reduction or shareholder returns
order book & pipeline: 100% order-backed manufacturing; top 15 customers (including Walmart, Target, Costco, TJMaxx) contribute >80% of revenue; customer demand pipeline estimated at 10x current capacity
segment / subsidiary detail: Floor Coverings: INR 550 Cr capacity, 55% utilisation; Top of Bed/Blankets: INR 500 Cr capacity, 60% utilisation; Performance/Outdoor: INR 450 Cr capacity, 55% utilisation; Handloom: INR 150 Cr capacity, 30% utilisation
growth verticals / optionality: MMF (micro polyester) segment expansion via PLI-funded capex; potential to capture 20x current export potential in MMF; diversification into EU/UK markets with tariff refunds; scaling with existing customers who seek 10x volume growth
margins & cost dynamics: EBIDTA margin rebounded to 13.25% in Q4FY26 (from 9.15% in Q3FY26); H1FY27 input cost pressure (cotton, polyester, logistics +25-35% due to US-Iran war) partially offset by USDINR and customer repricing; margins expected to improve with scale and tariff unwind
capex / expansion: INR 363.7 Cr cumulative capex since FY20; planned FY27 capex ~INR 75 Cr for new product capabilities; major capex cycle concluding FY27; total installed revenue capacity now INR 1,650+ Cr
capital allocation: At least 40-50% of CFO to be allocated to debt reduction, dividends, or working capital optimisation post-FY27; INR 25+ Cr already invested in ESG (solar, PNG, electric MHE); strong supplier partnerships with upfront payments
risks & watch-items: Input cost volatility (cotton, polyester, fuel); USDINR fluctuations; delays in PLI approval; geopolitical disruptions (West Asia); customer concentration risk (top 12 contribute 80%); tariff renegotiation risks
non-obvious takeaways: Company's factory replacement value >INR 800 Cr creates a de facto moat — new entrants cannot replicate scale or customer trust; 85% FOB exports mean minimal FX hedging needed; 20+ year relationships imply low churn and high switching costs

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.
